results.notes: Built the per-run ceiling behind two switches, both default off and read with the strict literal "true" parser. RunCeiling::resolve applies budget.rs precedence (a request cap is used where set, the org's ceiling fills unset, non-positive caps are no cap). Token caps count input plus output of metered calls only, so subscription calls add no spend and no tokens. CeilingTracker keeps the metered tokens and the sent warning, and emits run_ceiling_80 and run_ceiling_reached once each, on the usage_progress frame that first crosses. The RichEventSink holds one lock over the meter and the tracker. The closing answer frame is read from the turn's total, so the answer's own cost can trigger a warning. Under MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_CEILING_ENFORCE the tool loop breaks at the round boundary once a cap is reached, after queued input is delivered, appends a notice, and the answer still streams. The fallback answer frame also carries the ceiling. With every switch off the code path is unchanged: no tracker, no pricing, no extra keys. Wiring: lib.rs is not owned, so the module is declared inside the owned sse_events.rs with #[path], the same way sse.rs declares cache_telemetry. Its path is crate::sse_events::run_ceiling, and lib.rs needs no edit. Frontend: RunCostMeter.tsx is a ceiling-only component, because S4 is not built. It is not mounted, and the chat-client parse of the new keys is in a shared file. Nothing committed or pushed. The worktree also holds uncommitted edits from WS24-S9 and WS23-S8.code, which I did not touch.
